title: Goodness Gracious Great Balls of Twine

sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: We are waist deep in summer right now, which is a great time of year if you're in the podcast business.
sentences.zh: 我们现在正处于盛夏时节，如果你从事播客行业，这可是个好时候。

sentences.en: Because it's road trip season.
sentences.zh: 因为这是公路旅行的季节。

sentences.en: Time to hop in the car, cue up your favorite podcasts.
sentences.zh: 是时候跳上车，播放你最喜欢的播客了。

sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: And hit the road.
sentences.zh: 然后踏上旅程。

sentences.en: That's producer Vivian Lee, and we recently sent her on a 1,200-mile road trip through the MidweSt.
sentences.zh: 那是制片人薇薇安·李，我们最近派她去中西部进行了一次1200英里的公路旅行。

sentences.en: And I saw a lot of things along the way.
sentences.zh: 沿途我看到了很多东西。

sentences.en: Bob Dylan's childhood home, a guitar made out of a bedpan, the inside of about 400 boxes of Chicken McNuggets, lots of horses.
sentences.zh: 鲍勃·迪伦的童年故居，一把用便盆做的吉他，大约400盒麦乐鸡的内包装，还有很多马。

sentences.en: Horses!
sentences.zh: 马！

sentences.en: But we didn't send Vivian out to look for horses, or to check a few states off her bucket liSt.
sentences.zh: 但我们派薇薇安出去并不是为了看马，也不是为了去完成她遗愿清单上的几个州。

sentences.en: She was on a mission that required equal parts science, philosophy, and daring.
sentences.zh: 她肩负着一项任务，这项任务需要科学、哲学和勇气的结合。

sentences.en: In search of something that's been hotly contested for decades.
sentences.zh: 去寻找一个几十年来一直备受争议的东西。

sentences.en: The world's largest ball of twine.
sentences.zh: 世界上最大的麻绳球。

sentences.en: I began my quest by following in the footsteps of the great Weird Al Yankovic.
sentences.zh: 我追随伟大的“怪人”阿尔·扬科维奇的脚步，开始了我的探索。

sentences.en: We want to see the biggest ball of twine in Minnesota.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看明尼苏达州最大的麻绳球。

sentences.en: To a twine ball I heard about in Minnesota.
sentences.zh: 去看看我在明尼苏达州听说的一个麻绳球。

sentences.en: The biggest ball of twine in Minnesota.
sentences.zh: 明尼苏达州最大的麻绳球。

sentences.en: About an hour west of St. Paul is a tiny little city called Darwin.
sentences.zh: 在圣保罗以西约一小时车程的地方，有一个叫达尔文的小镇。

sentences.en: It isn't the kind of place you'd expect to find a great wonder of the world.
sentences.zh: 这可不是你会期望找到世界奇迹的地方。

sentences.en: The population is only about 350.
sentences.zh: 人口只有350人左右。

sentences.en: I accidentally circled the entire downtown in about two minutes while looking for parking.
sentences.zh: 我找停车位时，不小心绕着整个市中心转了两分钟。

sentences.en: The main street is only three blocks long.
sentences.zh: 主街只有三个街区长。

sentences.en: There's a bank, a water tower, and a nine-ton ball of twine entombed in a plexiglass gazebo.
sentences.zh: 那里有一家银行、一座水塔，还有一个被封存在有机玻璃凉亭里的九吨重麻绳球。

sentences.en: So it says, uh, world's largest ball of twine made by one man.
sentences.zh: 上面写着，呃，由一人制作的世界上最大的麻绳球。

sentences.en: It's very round.
sentences.zh: 它非常圆。

sentences.en: Very round and nicely shaped.
sentences.zh: 非常圆，形状很好。

sentences.en: It's hard to get a good look from the outside because of the reflection of the glass.
sentences.zh: 因为玻璃的反光，从外面很难看清楚。

sentences.en: But once you press your face up against those windows,
sentences.zh: 但一旦你把脸贴在窗户上，

sentences.en: you'll see this enormous, perfectly round orb that's comprised of brown twine.
sentences.zh: 你就会看到这个由棕色麻绳组成的巨大、完美的球体。

sentences.en: The ball is the pride of Darwin.
sentences.zh: 这个球是达尔文的骄傲。

sentences.en: But before Courtney Johnson moved here, she had never even heard of it.
sentences.zh: 但在考特尼·约翰逊搬到这里之前，她甚至从未听说过它。

sentences.en: When I first came to the area, I didn't know anything about the twine ball.
sentences.zh: 我刚到这个地区时，对麻绳球一无所知。

sentences.en: Johnson's husband grew up in Darwin, so she asked him.
sentences.zh: 约翰逊的丈夫在达尔文长大，所以她问了他。

sentences.en: I was like, what is this?
sentences.zh: 我当时问，这是什么？

sentences.en: And he's like, it's the twine ball.
sentences.zh: 他说，这是麻绳球。

sentences.en: And I kind of laughed at it because it is kind of silly if you think about it.
sentences.zh: 我当时笑了，因为如果你仔细想想，这确实有点傻。

sentences.en: And he's like, don't laugh because we're related to them.
sentences.zh: 他说，别笑，因为我们和他们有亲戚关系。

sentences.en: Courtney's husband is a distant nephew of Francis Johnson,
sentences.zh: 考特尼的丈夫是弗朗西斯·约翰逊的远房侄孙，

sentences.en: the man who rolled the Darwin twine ball.
sentences.zh: 也就是那个滚动达尔文麻绳球的人。

sentences.en: And she and her husband actually inherited the Johnson family farm.
sentences.zh: 她和丈夫实际上继承了约翰逊家族的农场。

sentences.en: Which is where the story of great-great-uncle Francis and his giant ball of twine begins.
sentences.zh: 而这正是曾曾叔祖父弗朗西斯和他巨大麻绳球故事开始的地方。

sentences.en: I'd like to tell you that Francis Johnson had a vision of doing something majestic,
sentences.zh: 我很想告诉你，弗朗西斯·约翰逊当时有一个宏伟的愿景，

sentences.en: rolling the largest ball of twine the country had ever seen.
sentences.zh: 要滚动出全国见过的最大的麻绳球。

sentences.en: But the truth is, he just had too much twine lying around.
sentences.zh: 但事实是，他只是手头有太多多余的麻绳。

sentences.en: Johnson was a farmer, and his farm, like all farms really, was lousy with twine.
sentences.zh: 约翰逊是个农民，他的农场，实际上像所有农场一样，到处都是麻绳。

sentences.en: And one day in 1950, while cleaning up after his nephew Harlan,
sentences.zh: 1950年的一天，在清理他侄子哈兰留下的烂摊子时，

sentences.en: Johnson started rolling some of that extra twine into a ball.
sentences.zh: 约翰逊开始把一些多余的麻绳卷成一个球。

sentences.en: So he, of course, picked up the twine, yelling at Harlan that he's just young
sentences.zh: 所以他当然捡起了麻绳，冲哈兰大喊，说他还年轻，

sentences.en: and needs to start picking up after himself.
sentences.zh: 需要学会自己收拾残局。

sentences.en: Well, before you know it, he had, you know, a six-inch twine ball.
sentences.zh: 好吧，不知不觉中，他就有了，你知道，一个六英寸大的麻绳球。

sentences.en: Well, the six-inch twine ball would get into a foot.
sentences.zh: 嗯，六英寸的麻绳球会变成一英尺。

sentences.en: And for reasons unknown even to himself,
sentences.zh: 出于连他自己都不知道的原因，

sentences.en: Johnson rolled that ball of twine for the next 29 years.
sentences.zh: 约翰逊在接下来的29年里一直在滚动那个麻绳球。

sentences.en: The twine ball was easy enough to roll in its early stages.
sentences.zh: 麻绳球在早期阶段很容易滚动。

sentences.en: Johnson would work on it in the basement.
sentences.zh: 约翰逊会在地下室里处理它。

sentences.en: But as it got bigger, he had to move the ball outside or it'd get stuck down there for good.
sentences.zh: 但随着它变大，他不得不把球移到外面，否则它就会永远卡在那里。

sentences.en: Here's an interview with Johnson from an early 80s TV show called Real People.
sentences.zh: 这是一段80年代初电视节目《真实的人》中对约翰逊的采访。

sentences.en: I had to roll it out of the basement while I could still get it through a 30-inch door.
sentences.zh: 我趁还能把它通过30英寸的门时，就把它滚出了地下室。

sentences.en: And it's been outdoors ever since.
sentences.zh: 从那以后它就一直放在户外。

sentences.en: And it was outdoors on his front lawn that he rolled it for four hours a day, every single day.
sentences.zh: 它在门前的草坪上，他每天花四个小时滚动它，每一天都是如此。

sentences.en: It became an addiction and obsession.
sentences.zh: 这成了一种瘾和痴迷。

sentences.en: And it was something that he wanted to do because it sparked something inside of him.
sentences.zh: 这是他想做的事情，因为它点燃了他内心的某种东西。

sentences.en: Francis Johnson was a perfectioniSt.
sentences.zh: 弗朗西斯·约翰逊是个完美主义者。

sentences.en: And he was adamant that his twine ball should be a perfectly round sphere.
sentences.zh: 他坚持认为他的麻绳球应该是一个完美的球体。

sentences.en: As it got bigger, he rolled it around the yard to make sure he added twine evenly.
sentences.zh: 随着它变大，他会在院子里滚动它，以确保他均匀地添加麻绳。

sentences.en: So it remained beautifully symmetrical.
sentences.zh: 所以它保持了美丽的对称性。

sentences.en: But eventually, the ball got so big that he couldn't roll it around his yard anymore with just his body weight.
sentences.zh: 但最终，球变得太大了，他仅靠自己的体重无法再在院子里滚动它了。

sentences.en: And so Johnson invented an ingenious method to rotate the ball using railroad jacks.
sentences.zh: 于是约翰逊发明了一种巧妙的方法，利用铁路千斤顶来旋转球体。

sentences.en: He would tuck a jack under the ball and use it to nudge the ball forward.
sentences.zh: 他会把千斤顶塞在球下面，用它来推动球向前移动。

sentences.en: And then the twine ball would roll.
sentences.zh: 然后麻绳球就会滚动。

sentences.en: And of course, on the other side of it, he would have something to stop the ball from rolling completely.
sentences.zh: 当然，在球的另一边，他会放些东西来阻止球完全滚走。

sentences.en: He repeated this process over and over.
sentences.zh: 他一遍又一遍地重复这个过程。

sentences.en: Rolling the ball, adding twine, rolling the ball, adding more twine.
sentences.zh: 滚动球，添加麻绳，滚动球，添加更多麻绳。

sentences.en: He rolled it around his yard.
sentences.zh: 他在院子里滚动它。

sentences.en: He chained it to a tree so no one would steal the twine ball.
sentences.zh: 他把它锁在树上，这样就不会有人偷走麻绳球。

sentences.en: I mean, who would steal the twine ball?
sentences.zh: 我是说，谁会偷麻绳球呢？

sentences.en: But that was the way he was.
sentences.zh: 但这就是他的行事风格。

sentences.en: The ball attracted a lot of attention both in and out of Darwin.
sentences.zh: 这个球在达尔文内外都吸引了很多关注。

sentences.en: It appeared on television, got written about in newspapers, and Weird Al would eventually write a song about it.
sentences.zh: 它出现在电视上，被报纸报道，后来“怪人”阿尔还为它写了一首歌。

sentences.en: The ball had made Johnson famous, even if he wasn't willing to admit it.
sentences.zh: 这个球让约翰逊出了名，即使他并不愿意承认。

sentences.en: Well, I don't know about that, about being famous.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我不知道关于出名这件事。

sentences.en: I'm a modest little guy from the sticks.
sentences.zh: 我只是个来自乡下的谦虚小人物。

sentences.en: So, uh, they gotta take me as I am.
sentences.zh: 所以，呃，他们得接受本来的我。

sentences.en: Francis' twine ball was absolutely massive.
sentences.zh: 弗朗西斯的麻绳球绝对是巨大的。

sentences.en: It had to be the largest ball of twine in the world.
sentences.zh: 它一定是世界上最大的麻绳球。

sentences.en: So, that's what he called it.
sentences.zh: 所以，他就是这么称呼它的。

sentences.en: This is the biggest ball of twine in the world because there's no one come forth with a bigger one.
sentences.zh: 这是世界上最大的麻绳球，因为还没有人拿出更大的来。

sentences.en: Until someone did.
sentences.zh: 直到有人做到了。

sentences.en: I'm Linda Clover.
sentences.zh: 我是琳达·克洛弗。

sentences.en: I live in Cocker City, Kansas, and I'm the caretaker of the world's largest ball of twine.
sentences.zh: 我住在堪萨斯州的科克城，我是世界上最大的麻绳球的看管人。

sentences.en: Cocker City is about 500 miles south of Darwin.
sentences.zh: 科克城在达尔文以南约500英里处。

sentences.en: They, too, have a massive ball of twine.
sentences.zh: 他们也有一个巨大的麻绳球。

sentences.en: And it's Linda's job to look after it.
sentences.zh: 照顾它是琳达的工作。

sentences.en: The Wall Street Journal called me the bell of the ball.
sentences.zh: 《华尔街日报》称我为“球之美人”。

sentences.en: But to some local people, I think I'm the crazy twine lady.
sentences.zh: 但对一些当地人来说，我想我是那个疯狂的麻绳女士。

sentences.en: Cocker City's population is a little larger than Darwin's.
sentences.zh: 科克城的人口比达尔文稍微多一点。

sentences.en: But walking around, you wouldn't guess it.
sentences.zh: 但走在街上，你不会这么觉得。

sentences.en: It almost felt like an empty set of a Western movie.
sentences.zh: 它感觉几乎就像西部电影的空置布景。

sentences.en: And in some of the windows of the abandoned storefronts, there's twine ball-inspired artwork.
sentences.zh: 在一些废弃店面的窗户里，有一些受麻绳球启发的艺术品。

sentences.en: The Mona Lisa holding a twine ball.
sentences.zh: 蒙娜丽莎手里拿着一个麻绳球。

sentences.en: And one of Georgia O'Keeffe's flowers with the twine ball at the center.
sentences.zh: 还有一朵乔治亚·欧姬芙的花，中心是麻绳球。

sentences.en: We have things going on, but not much.
sentences.zh: 我们这里有活动，但不多。

sentences.en: But that's okay.
sentences.zh: 但没关系。

sentences.en: We have beautiful sunrises and sunsets.
sentences.zh: 我们有美丽的日出和日落。

sentences.en: And the wonderful lake.
sentences.zh: 还有美妙的湖泊。

sentences.en: They also have an absolutely gigantic twine ball sitting under an open-air gazebo right in the center of town.
sentences.zh: 他们还有一个巨大的麻绳球，放在镇中心的一个露天凉亭下。

sentences.en: And unlike its counterpart in Darwin, which is trapped behind glass, this one you can walk right up to and touch.
sentences.zh: 与达尔文那个被困在玻璃后面的球不同，这个你可以直接走过去触摸。

sentences.en: We want people to be able to smell it because twine has its own fragrance.
sentences.zh: 我们希望人们能闻到它，因为麻绳有它自己的香味。

sentences.en: It certainly does.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Ooh, it's got a smell.
sentences.zh: 噢，它有味道。

sentences.en: Ooh, it smells moiSt.
sentences.zh: 噢，闻起来潮潮的。

sentences.en: Linda Clover may be the caretaker of the Cocker City twine ball, but it was rolled by a man named Frank Stober.
sentences.zh: 琳达·克洛弗可能是科克城麻绳球的看管人，但它是弗兰克·斯托伯滚动出来的。

sentences.en: Stober started in 1953, coincidentally right around the same time that Johnson was getting going up in Minnesota.
sentences.zh: 斯托伯在1953年开始，巧合的是，这正是约翰逊在明尼苏达州开始的时候。

sentences.en: Amazingly, two men about the same time, one in Minnesota and one man from Kansas, did twine balls.
sentences.zh: 令人惊奇的是，两个人几乎在同一时间，一个在明尼苏达州，一个来自堪萨斯州，都做了麻绳球。

sentences.en: Stober was a farmer, just like Francis Johnson, and he got started rolling his ball of twine in basically the exact same way that Johnson did.
sentences.zh: 斯托伯和弗朗西斯·约翰逊一样是个农民，他开始滚动麻绳球的方式基本上和约翰逊一模一样。

sentences.en: He started it because he was cleaning up his barn.
sentences.zh: 他开始是因为他在清理谷仓。

sentences.en: And the man just was picking up the twine because it was on his barn floor, thinking he would roll it into a ball, put it into a tub to get it out of the way.
sentences.zh: 那个人只是捡起麻绳，因为它就在谷仓地板上，想着把它卷成球，放进桶里，以免碍事。

sentences.en: Stober and Johnson were both raised with a Depression-era reluctance to waste anything at all.
sentences.zh: 斯托伯和约翰逊都是在经济大萧条时期长大的，对浪费任何东西都有一种抵触情绪。

sentences.en: Except for time.
sentences.zh: 除了时间。

sentences.en: And Stober may not have been the first person to try to roll the world's biggest twine ball, but he certainly had a talent for it.
sentences.zh: 斯托伯可能不是第一个尝试滚动世界最大麻绳球的人，但他确实有这方面的天赋。

sentences.en: By 1956, just three years in, Stober's ball was already seven and a half feet tall and weighed over 4,000 pounds, nearly the size of the Darwin twine ball.
sentences.zh: 到1956年，仅仅三年时间，斯托伯的球就已经有七英尺半高，重达4000多磅，几乎和达尔文的麻绳球一样大。

sentences.en: I think it starts with people maybe making fun of them because it's such a ludicrous thing, but then you quickly realize there's something about them that, you know,
sentences.zh: 我想这始于人们可能嘲笑他们，因为这是一件如此荒谬的事情，但你很快就会意识到他们身上有一些东西，你知道，

sentences.en: it's somebody who took what should have been insignificant little pieces of twine or string or garbage,
sentences.zh: 这是一个把本应是微不足道的麻绳、细绳或垃圾碎片的人，

sentences.en: and they'd made something that's essentially made them immortal.
sentences.zh: 他们创造了一些本质上让他们永垂不朽的东西。

sentences.en: This is Doug Kirby, the co-founder of Roadside America, which is a website dedicated to documenting the quirky, kooky, and kitschy roadside attractions along our highways.
sentences.zh: 这是道格·柯比，Roadside America的联合创始人，这是一个致力于记录我们高速公路沿线古怪、离奇和媚俗的路边景点的网站。

sentences.en: The balls are pretty much a pilgrimage site for different groups now because you really can't go through Minnesota or Kansas and not detour to see those balls.
sentences.zh: 这些球现在几乎成了不同群体的朝圣地，因为你真的不能穿过明尼苏达州或堪萨斯州而不绕道去看看这些球。

sentences.en: Kirby's been tracking the status of the balls for a long time.
sentences.zh: 柯比长期以来一直在追踪这些球的状态。

sentences.en: And when I went to meet with him, he even sketched out a little cartoon timeline for me.
sentences.zh: 当我见到他时，他甚至为我画了一个小卡通时间轴。

sentences.en: He says that for a stretch of time, it looked like Stober's ball in Cocker City might have taken the lead.
sentences.zh: 他说，有一段时间，看起来科克城的斯托伯球可能领先了。

sentences.en: There's no record, and we have our speculation on the website, which was that Cocker City's hit 11 feet in 861.
sentences.zh: 没有记录，我们在网站上有我们的推测，那就是科克城的球在1961年达到了11英尺。

sentences.en: By this point, Stober's ball had become a popular attraction in central Kansas.
sentences.zh: 到这一点时，斯托伯的球已经成为堪萨斯州中部的一个热门景点。

sentences.en: He would take it to local fairs and people would try to guess the weight.
sentences.zh: 他会把它带到当地的集市上，人们会尝试猜测它的重量。

sentences.en: It was such a hit that town officials asked Stober if he could bring the twine ball into the town to put it on permanent display.
sentences.zh: 它太受欢迎了，以至于镇官员问斯托伯是否可以把麻绳球带进镇里进行永久展示。

sentences.en: And then finally, after decades of speculation, the world's largest ball of twine became official in pretty much the only way these sorts of things can.
sentences.zh: 最后，经过几十年的猜测，世界上最大的麻绳球以这种事情唯一可能的方式成为了官方认证。

sentences.en: Yes, it was in the Guinness Book of World Records.
sentences.zh: 是的，它被列入了《吉尼斯世界纪录大全》。

sentences.en: Officials from the Guinness Book of World Records came to Cocker City, Kansas in 1973 and declared Stober's ball the official world's largest ball of twine at 11 feet in diameter.
sentences.zh: 《吉尼斯世界纪录大全》的官员于1973年来到堪萨斯州科克城，宣布斯托伯的球为官方认定的世界上最大的麻绳球，直径为11英尺。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, his glory was short-lived because he died the following year in 1974.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，他的荣耀很短暂，因为他在第二年，即1974年去世了。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, up in Darwin, Minnesota, Johnson was still alive and kicking and rolling twine.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，在明尼苏达州的达尔文，约翰逊还活着，并且还在滚动麻绳。

sentences.en: He kept going until he surpassed Stober's ball and dethroned Cocker City for the Guinness World Record just a few years later.
sentences.zh: 他一直坚持，直到几年后超过了斯托伯的球，并从科克城手中夺回了吉尼斯世界纪录。

sentences.en: And without anyone left to challenge his place in history, Johnson retired from twine ball rolling.
sentences.zh: 在没有人能挑战他在历史上的地位后，约翰逊从滚动麻绳球中退休了。

sentences.en: He died 10 years later from emphysema at the age of 85.
sentences.zh: 10年后，他因肺气肿去世，享年85岁。

sentences.en: It was a lung disease that did kill him.
sentences.zh: 这是一种夺走他生命的肺部疾病。

sentences.en: And you look at family history, there is no history of it.
sentences.zh: 你看家族史，并没有这种病史。

sentences.en: So a lot of people say it was inhaling twine and chemicals and all that throughout those years.
sentences.zh: 所以很多人说是因为那些年吸入了麻绳和化学物质等等。

sentences.en: That probably was the reason of his death.
sentences.zh: 那很可能是他死亡的原因。

sentences.en: His family contends that Johnson's lifelong passion ultimately killed him.
sentences.zh: 他的家人认为，约翰逊终身的激情最终夺走了他的生命。

sentences.en: Yeah, but I don't think he'd change anything.
sentences.zh: 是啊，但我不认为他会改变任何事情。

sentences.en: If someone were to tell him, you know, you're going to die from this, he'd be like, so?
sentences.zh: 如果有人告诉他，你知道吗，你会因为这个而死，他会说，那又怎样？

sentences.en: And he would keep doing it.
sentences.zh: 然后他会继续做下去。

sentences.en: And the story could have ended there, with two dead twine men, the largest ball of twine in the world, and the second largest ball of twine in the world.
sentences.zh: 故事本可以到此为止：两个死去的麻绳球制造者，世界第一大麻绳球，以及世界第二大麻绳球。

sentences.en: But Cocker City wasn't finished yet.
sentences.zh: 但科克市还没打算就此罢休。

sentences.en: Stober had left the twine ball to the city after he died.
sentences.zh: 斯托伯去世后，把那个麻绳球留给了这座城市。

sentences.en: And for a few years, it just sat there in the downtown gazebo, a tribute to the second greatest twine ball roller in history.
sentences.zh: 几年里，它就一直静静地待在市中心的凉亭里，作为对历史上第二伟大的麻绳球制造者的致敬。

sentences.en: But then the town decided they didn't want to settle for second beSt.
sentences.zh: 但后来，镇上的人决定他们不想只满足于第二名。

sentences.en: We decided, let's have some fun.
sentences.zh: 我们决定，不如找点乐子。

sentences.en: And we started having what we call our annual twine-a-thon.
sentences.zh: 于是我们开始举办所谓的年度“麻绳马拉松”。

sentences.en: Residents of Cocker City decided to jump in and start adding more twine to the Stober Ball to see if they could beat the record again.
sentences.zh: 科克市的居民决定加入进来，开始往斯托伯的球上缠更多的麻绳，看看能否再次打破纪录。

sentences.en: But this time, it wouldn't be the product of one man, but an entire community.
sentences.zh: 但这一次，它不再是一个人的作品，而是一个社区的结晶。

sentences.en: The town had what was a brilliant idea, which was let's let the community keep rolling in.
sentences.zh: 镇上想出了一个绝妙的主意，那就是让社区的人继续缠下去。

sentences.en: Here's Doug Kirby from Roadside America again.
sentences.zh: 这是来自“美国路边”的道格·柯比。

sentences.en: He says that Cocker City started holding twine-a-thons once a year, where everyone in town would gather to help grow the twine ball.
sentences.zh: 他说科克市开始每年举办一次“麻绳马拉松”，全镇的人都会聚在一起，帮助那个麻绳球长大。

sentences.en: And eventually, they started allowing visitors to wrap the twine ball on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 最终，他们开始允许游客每天也来缠上一圈。

sentences.en: Getting to wrap the twine ball became the reason to visit Cocker City.
sentences.zh: 能亲手缠上那个麻绳球，成了人们造访科克市的理由。

sentences.en: So whether it was townspeople or visitors, and let's just have the ball set up so that the spool's ready, you can add to the ball,
sentences.zh: 所以无论是镇民还是游客，我们把球架好，线轴准备好，你就可以往球上加绳子了，

sentences.en: you'll see immediately that you're adding to this world record.
sentences.zh: 你会立刻看到，你正在为这个世界纪录添砖加瓦。

sentences.en: So it's a different approach.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一种不同的方式。

sentences.en: Linda Clover literally keeps spools of twine on her at all times, on the off chance that she runs into someone who wants to add to the ball.
sentences.zh: 琳达·克洛弗随时随地都带着线轴，以防万一遇到想往球上加绳子的人。

sentences.en: If you go to my car or my pickup truck, either one has twine that I have ready to let people add twine onto the ball.
sentences.zh: 如果你去我的车或皮卡车里看看，里面都有我准备好的麻绳，让人们可以往球上缠。

sentences.en: Now, no one else in town carries twine with them, but Linda Clover does.
sentences.zh: 镇上没别人随身带着麻绳，但琳达·克洛弗会。

sentences.en: With so many people participating, the Cocker City ball continues to grow bigger and bigger.
sentences.zh: 随着参与的人越来越多，科克市的麻绳球变得越来越大。

sentences.en: The latest estimate has it at 20,500 pounds, over 2,500 pounds heavier than Johnson's.
sentences.zh: 最新的估计重量是20500磅，比约翰逊的球重了2500多磅。

sentences.en: And when you see it in person, it's unquestionably larger in circumference.
sentences.zh: 当你亲眼看到它时，它的周长确实更大。

sentences.en: But not everyone agrees that rolling twine balls should be a group project, especially in Darwin.
sentences.zh: 但并不是所有人都认为缠麻绳球应该是一项集体项目，尤其是在达尔文镇。

sentences.en: Courtney says that Johnson's ball is particularly impressive, not just because of its perfectly round shape,
sentences.zh: 考特尼说，约翰逊的球特别令人印象深刻，不仅是因为它完美的圆形，

sentences.en: but because it was the sole accomplishment of one man.
sentences.zh: 还因为它是一个人独自完成的成就。

sentences.en: It needed to be done by him because it needed to be perfect.
sentences.zh: 它必须由他来完成，因为它必须完美无瑕。

sentences.en: It needed to be solid.
sentences.zh: 它必须坚实稳固。

sentences.en: It needed to be done with only a certain type of twine.
sentences.zh: 它必须只用特定类型的麻绳来完成。

sentences.en: You know, he was just so particular and needed things done by himself.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他就是那么挑剔，凡事都得亲力亲为。

sentences.en: And remember, Johnson had his own special technique for rolling a perfectly symmetrical sphere.
sentences.zh: 别忘了，约翰逊有他自己缠绕完美对称球体的独特技巧。

sentences.en: The people of Cocker City don't have that.
sentences.zh: 科克市的人没有那种技巧。

sentences.en: They have no way to wrap the top and the bottom of the ball, so it just keeps getting wider and wider.
sentences.zh: 他们没法缠好球的顶部和底部，所以它只会变得越来越宽。

sentences.en: In fact, it's not really a ball anymore, more an oval with a flat bottom.
sentences.zh: 事实上，它已经不再是个球了，更像是一个底部平坦的椭圆体。

sentences.en: So Cocker City's ball might be bigger, but the Darwin ball is definitely nicer to look at.
sentences.zh: 所以科克市的球可能更大，但达尔文的球绝对更好看。

sentences.en: Darwin is by far my favorite ball.
sentences.zh: 达尔文的球是我目前为止最喜欢的。

sentences.en: This is Edward Meyer, and he's currently retired.
sentences.zh: 这位是爱德华·迈耶，他现在已经退休了。

sentences.en: But up until a year ago, he had probably the coolest job I'd ever heard of.
sentences.zh: 但在一年以前，他可能拥有我听说过的最酷的工作。

sentences.en: My primary focus was to buy exhibits to put in the museums, which Ripley's calls auditoriums, spelled O-D-D, around the world.
sentences.zh: 我的主要工作是购买展品，放到世界各地的博物馆里，雷普利公司称之为“奇趣馆”，拼写是O-D-D。

sentences.en: Meyer was vice president of exhibits and archives with Ripley's Believe It or Not,
sentences.zh: 迈耶曾是“雷普利信不信由你”博物馆的展品与档案副总裁，

sentences.en: meaning it was literally his job to find the weirdest things in the world and put them on display.
sentences.zh: 这意味着他的工作就是去寻找世界上最奇怪的东西并将其展示出来。

sentences.en: And back in the early 90s, he had his eye on Darwin's giant twine ball.
sentences.zh: 早在90年代初，他就盯上了达尔文的巨型麻绳球。

sentences.en: The Darwin ball, you know, it's almost romantic.
sentences.zh: 达尔文的球，你知道，它几乎带有一种浪漫色彩。

sentences.en: It's one man's dream, and it takes him a long time, and he has certain rules that he plays by and doesn't break.
sentences.zh: 这是一个人的梦想，他花了很长时间，并且遵守着自己定下的规矩，从不打破。

sentences.en: And, you know, it's, you know, I'm getting silly, I guess.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我猜我有点傻了。

sentences.en: But, you know, it's an accomplishment like climbing EvereSt.
sentences.zh: 但你知道，这就像攀登珠穆朗玛峰一样，是一项了不起的成就。

sentences.en: Meyer had been interested in the Darwin twine ball for years, and as luck would have it,
sentences.zh: 迈耶多年来一直对达尔文的麻绳球很感兴趣，巧合的是，

sentences.en: Johnson's nephew had inherited his entire estate, including the twine ball.
sentences.zh: 约翰逊的侄子继承了他的全部遗产，包括那个麻绳球。

sentences.en: Johnson's nephew called Meyer up one day to ask if he wanted to come to Darwin and possibly purchase the ball for Ripley's.
sentences.zh: 有一天，约翰逊的侄子打电话给迈耶，问他是否想来达尔文，并可能把这个球买给雷普利博物馆。

sentences.en: He invited me, and I said, sure, I'd love to come.
sentences.zh: 他邀请了我，我说，当然，我很乐意去。

sentences.en: Meyer was asked to pitch the town on the idea of putting Johnson's twine ball in a Ripley's museum.
sentences.zh: 迈耶被要求向镇上推销把约翰逊的麻绳球放进雷普利博物馆的想法。

sentences.en: And personally, he thought, what better way to honor Johnson's accomplishment than to put it on display where possibly thousands of people a week would see it.
sentences.zh: 他个人认为，把约翰逊的成就展示出来，让每周成千上万的人看到，是对他最好的纪念。

sentences.en: I gave a presentation and told them that I wanted to buy it, and the reaction was, you know, over our dead body.
sentences.zh: 我做了一个演示，告诉他们我想买下它，结果他们的反应是，你知道，除非我们死了。

sentences.en: It was probably one of the most uncomfortable evenings of my entire life.
sentences.zh: 那可能是我一生中最尴尬的夜晚之一。

sentences.en: Uh, I was literally in fear of my life.
sentences.zh: 呃，我当时真的担心自己的生命安全。

sentences.en: I was not sure how this was going to end.
sentences.zh: 我不确定这会如何收场。

sentences.en: Spoiler alert, he wasn't murdered by a mob of angry townspeople.
sentences.zh: 剧透一下，他并没有被愤怒的镇民暴徒谋杀。

sentences.en: But they were pretty upset.
sentences.zh: 但他们确实非常生气。

sentences.en: For one, the people of Darwin thought the twine ball could bring in tourism to the area.
sentences.zh: 首先，达尔文的人认为这个麻绳球能为当地带来旅游业。

sentences.en: But more importantly, the ball had become part of Darwin's identity.
sentences.zh: 但更重要的是，这个球已经成为了达尔文身份认同的一部分。

sentences.en: Twine ball is a good analogy, we say.
sentences.zh: 我们常说，麻绳球是一个很好的比喻。

sentences.en: It's the twine that binds, it represents, you know, not only how we support that, but our support of each other.
sentences.zh: 是麻绳将我们紧紧连在一起，它不仅代表了我们如何支持它，也代表了我们对彼此的支持。

sentences.en: This is Josh Johnson, the mayor of Darwin.
sentences.zh: 这位是乔什·约翰逊，达尔文的镇长。

sentences.en: The town had adopted the ball as their own so much so that they even started an annual tradition called Darwin Twine Ball Day,
sentences.zh: 镇上的人已经把这个球当成了他们自己的东西，甚至还发起了一个名为“达尔文麻绳球日”的年度传统，

sentences.en: which includes a number of twine ball-related activities like a twine-K, which is kind of like a 5K.
sentences.zh: 其中包括许多与麻绳球相关的活动，比如“麻绳5公里跑”，有点像5公里长跑。

sentences.en: It starts out with a 17,400-foot run.
sentences.zh: 它以17400英尺的跑步开始。

sentences.en: That's a 17,400-foot run to celebrate a 17,400-pound twine ball.
sentences.zh: 那是为了庆祝一个17400磅重的麻绳球而进行的17400英尺长跑。

sentences.en: They pass out candy to kids, roll miniature versions of the twine ball down the street, and have a parade.
sentences.zh: 他们给孩子们分发糖果，把迷你版的麻绳球滚下街头，还举行游行。

sentences.en: It probably lasts around 35 minutes, which is the right length for a parade these days, in my opinion.
sentences.zh: 它大概持续35分钟，在我看来，这是如今游行合适的长度。

sentences.en: Francis Johnson's ball had become central to life in Darwin.
sentences.zh: 弗朗西斯·约翰逊的球已经成为达尔文生活的核心。

sentences.en: And Darwin made it clear that if Meyer wanted a giant twine ball for Ripley's, he would have to get it from some other town.
sentences.zh: 达尔文明确表示，如果迈耶想为雷普利博物馆找一个巨型麻绳球，他得去别的镇上找。

sentences.en: And that's exactly what Edward Meyer did.
sentences.zh: 而这正是爱德华·迈耶所做的。

sentences.en: Well, I literally read it in an airplane magazine, that this guy in Texas had been inspired as much by Cocker City as he had been by Darwin.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我是在一本飞机杂志上读到的，说德克萨斯州的这个家伙受到的启发既来自科克市，也来自达尔文。

sentences.en: As it turned out, while Darwin and Cocker City were battling it out in their public twine ball arms race,
sentences.zh: 事实证明，当达尔文和科克市在他们的公共麻绳球军备竞赛中斗得不可开交时，

sentences.en: a third ball was rapidly growing in Texas, at the hands of a man named J.C.
sentences.zh: 第三个球正在德克萨斯州迅速长大，出自一个名叫J.C.的人之手。

sentences.en: Payne.
sentences.zh: 佩恩。

sentences.en: Payne was a retired brick mason, who was the type of guy who was always in search of a new project.
sentences.zh: 佩恩是一位退休的砖瓦匠，他那种人总是热衷于寻找新的项目。

sentences.en: And in the late 1980s, he found one.
sentences.zh: 在80年代末，他找到了一个。

sentences.en: Payne had read about the Battle of the Balls in Darwin and Cocker City, and had a clear favorite in the race.
sentences.zh: 佩恩读过关于达尔文和科克市的“球之战”的报道，在比赛中他有明确的支持对象。

sentences.en: From the beginning, J.C.
sentences.zh: 从一开始，J.C.

sentences.en: Payne did not want Cocker City to beat Francis Johnson.
sentences.zh: 佩恩就不希望科克市打败弗朗西斯·约翰逊。

sentences.en: Apparently, Payne was not a fan of the fact that the Cocker City community effort was about to beat Johnson's solo project.
sentences.zh: 显然，佩恩不喜欢科克市的社区努力即将打败约翰逊个人项目的事实。

sentences.en: Payne believed in the great man theory of twine ball rolling.
sentences.zh: 佩恩相信麻绳球制造的“伟人理论”。

sentences.en: He thought, you know, that it was a shame that Cocker City was going to soon be bigger than Darwin's,
sentences.zh: 他想，你知道，科克市很快就要比达尔文的还要大，这真是一种遗憾，

sentences.en: because the whole town was involved in it.
sentences.zh: 因为那是全镇参与的结果。

sentences.en: And he thought that this was, you know, I used the word cheating, but that's, you know, my interpretation.
sentences.zh: 他认为这，你知道，我用了“作弊”这个词，但那是，你知道，我的解读。

sentences.en: And said, you know, if Francis isn't going to be the world's biggest, then I'm going to be the world's biggeSt.
sentences.zh: 他说，你知道，如果弗朗西斯不能成为世界第一，那我就要成为世界第一。

sentences.en: Payne didn't start rolling his ball until 1987, a full 37 years after Johnson.
sentences.zh: 佩恩直到1987年才开始缠他的球，比约翰逊晚了整整37年。

sentences.en: But by 1992, the Guinness Book of World Records declared it the largest ball in the world.
sentences.zh: 但到了1992年，《吉尼斯世界纪录大全》宣布它是世界上最大的球。

sentences.en: In a few short years, Payne managed to create a ball that was 42 feet in circumference, 13 feet tall, and weighed six tons.
sentences.zh: 在短短几年内，佩恩成功制造了一个周长42英尺、高13英尺、重达6吨的球。

sentences.en: Part of it is that he had a tool and used technology to add the string to it.
sentences.zh: 部分原因是他有工具，并利用技术手段往上面加绳子。

sentences.en: He had a tractor, he had a hook-type implement that, you know, prevented him from getting his hands wrecked,
sentences.zh: 他有一台拖拉机，还有一个钩状的工具，你知道，这让他不用把手弄坏，

sentences.en: that he wasn't literally even touching it at some point.
sentences.zh: 甚至在某些时候，他根本不需要亲手去碰它。

sentences.en: Part of it was that he, you know, used whatever he could get in terms of string, nylon specifically.
sentences.zh: 部分原因是他，你知道，利用他能弄到的任何绳子，特别是尼龙绳。

sentences.en: Which bothered a lot of twine ball purists who like to think of twine in the more traditional, more natural sense.
sentences.zh: 这让许多喜欢从传统、自然的角度看待麻绳的“麻绳球纯粹主义者”感到困扰。

sentences.en: I've seen the pile of plastic.
sentences.zh: 我见过那堆塑料。

sentences.en: Here's Linda Clover from Cocker City again.
sentences.zh: 这是科克市的琳达·克洛弗。

sentences.en: They're completely, we're talking apples and oranges, you know, completely, something completely different.
sentences.zh: 它们完全是两码事，我们说的是苹果和橘子，你知道，完全是两样东西。

sentences.en: The main gripe about J.C.
sentences.zh: 对J.C.的主要抱怨是

sentences.en: Payne's ball was that he used artificial colored nylon twine,
sentences.zh: 佩恩的球使用了人造彩色尼龙绳，

sentences.en: while Johnson and Stober both used sisal twine.
sentences.zh: 而约翰逊和斯托伯用的都是剑麻绳。

sentences.en: Sisal is an earthy colored plant-based material and has that classic farm look.
sentences.zh: 剑麻是一种大地色系的植物基材料，有一种经典的农场风格。

sentences.en: Whereas nylon just looks like city slicker twine.
sentences.zh: 而尼龙看起来就像城里人的麻绳。

sentences.en: Nylon also weighs less, making Payne's ball much lighter than both Cocker City and Darwin's.
sentences.zh: 尼龙也更轻，使得佩恩的球比科克市和达尔文的球都要轻得多。

sentences.en: The end result was a multicolored, artificial, lighter weight monstrosity.
sentences.zh: 最终的结果是一个五颜六色、人造的、重量较轻的怪物。

sentences.en: And Edward Meyer from Ripley's had to have it.
sentences.zh: 而雷普利博物馆的爱德华·迈耶必须得到它。

sentences.en: My buying it was a backhanded, you know, I'll buy this because.
sentences.zh: 我买它是一种退而求其次，你知道，我会买这个是因为。

sentences.en: You know, I missed out the one I really wanted, but I can still get one.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我错过了我真正想要的那个，但我还能弄到一个。

sentences.en: So he flew to Valley View, Texas, to meet Payne in person and see the ball for himself.
sentences.zh: 于是他飞往德克萨斯州的瓦利维尤，亲自去见佩恩并看看那个球。

sentences.en: Nice man, salt of the earth, a little bit on the competitive side.
sentences.zh: 好人，脚踏实地，有点好胜心。

sentences.en: But, you know, just a basic farm type guy.
sentences.zh: 但，你知道，就是一个普通的农场汉子。

sentences.en: And his ball, when I first saw it, looked pretty darn good.
sentences.zh: 而他的球，我第一次看到时，看起来相当不错。

sentences.en: But it didn't look good for long.
sentences.zh: 但它没能保持太久的好状态。

sentences.en: Pretty soon they realized that they'd have to move this six-ton ball
sentences.zh: 很快他们意识到，他们必须把这个6吨重的球搬走，

sentences.en: to a new Ripley's Museum being built in Branson, Missouri.
sentences.zh: 搬到正在密苏里州布兰森建造的新雷普利博物馆。

sentences.en: Well, we dragged it out of the barn and that messed it up a little bit.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们把它从谷仓里拖出来，这让它有点受损。

sentences.en: And then we had to lift it by a crane, which messed it up more.
sentences.zh: 然后我们不得不动用起重机吊起它，这让它受损更严重了。

sentences.en: And then it was dropped onto a flatbed truck that flattened the bottom part of it.
sentences.zh: 接着它被扔到平板卡车上，把底部压扁了。

sentences.en: And then it was driven, you know, the roughly thousand miles to Branson, Missouri from Denton, Texas.
sentences.zh: 然后它被运送了，你知道，大约一千英里，从德克萨斯州的丹顿到密苏里州的布兰森。

sentences.en: Still, this misshapen monster of a ball was going to be the pièce de résistance of the new Ripley's Museum.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，这个变形的怪物球还是成为了新雷普利博物馆的压轴展品。

sentences.en: And the ball was so huge that the building had to be constructed around it.
sentences.zh: 而且这个球太大了，博物馆大楼不得不围着它建造。

sentences.en: And if for any reason they ever need to move it out of there,
sentences.zh: 如果因为什么原因他们需要把它移出去，

sentences.en: they'll either need to take the roof off or blast a hole in the wall.
sentences.zh: 他们要么得拆掉屋顶，要么得在墙上炸个洞。

sentences.en: Oh, wow.
sentences.zh: 噢，哇。

sentences.en: So, wow.
sentences.zh: 所以，哇。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's huge.
sentences.zh: 是啊，它太大了。

sentences.en: I went to see Payne's Twine Ball for myself at the Ripley's in Branson.
sentences.zh: 我亲自去布兰森的雷普利博物馆看了佩恩的麻绳球。

sentences.en: In person, it's a little blobby looking, like a ball of cookie dough that's been sitting out for too long.
sentences.zh: 亲眼看去，它有点像一团放得太久的饼干面团，看起来有点软塌塌的。

sentences.en: And it's comprised of shiny nylon strands every color of the rainbow.
sentences.zh: 它由闪闪发光的尼龙线组成，颜色涵盖了彩虹的所有颜色。

sentences.en: It's pretty impressive.
sentences.zh: 它确实令人印象深刻。

sentences.en: But it sits on display between an ornate miniature palace carved out of camel bone
sentences.zh: 但它陈列在一个用骆驼骨雕刻的华丽微型宫殿，

sentences.en: and a six-foot ship made entirely of jade.
sentences.zh: 和一艘完全由玉石制成的六英尺长船之间。

sentences.en: And honestly, both are so beautiful that they make the ball look a little pedestrian.
sentences.zh: 老实说，这两样东西都太美了，让这个球看起来有点平庸。

sentences.en: Not to mention something else I noticed.
sentences.zh: 更不用说我注意到的另一件事了。

sentences.en: So, I'm just noticing something right now,
sentences.zh: 所以，我刚才注意到一件事，

sentences.en: which is that on this sign, it doesn't say the world's largest twine ball.
sentences.zh: 那就是在这个牌子上，它没有写“世界上最大的麻绳球”。

sentences.en: It says world's largest string ball.
sentences.zh: 它写的是“世界上最大的绳球”。

sentences.en: So, it's not even technically designated as twine here at Ripley's.
sentences.zh: 所以，在雷普利这里，它甚至在技术上都没有被定性为麻绳。

sentences.en: And this might be why the Great American Twine Ball Contest or String Ball Contest is never going to get a satisfying clear-cut winner
sentences.zh: 这可能就是为什么“全美麻绳球大赛”或“绳球大赛”永远不会有一个令人满意的明确赢家，

sentences.en: because no one is ever going to agree on the rules of the conteSt.
sentences.zh: 因为没有人能就比赛规则达成一致。

sentences.en: But at this point, all of the contestants seem to be okay with a version of the story where everyone wins.
sentences.zh: 但在这一点上，所有的参赛者似乎都接受了一个每个人都是赢家的故事版本。

sentences.en: Each town has the largest twine ball, depending on what you mean by that.
sentences.zh: 每个镇都有最大的麻绳球，取决于你如何定义它。

sentences.en: Darwin's is the largest twine ball rolled by one man.
sentences.zh: 达尔文的是由一个人缠出的最大麻绳球。

sentences.en: Cocker City's is the largest ball of sisal twine.
sentences.zh: 科克市的是最大的剑麻绳球。

sentences.en: And J.C.
sentences.zh: 而J.C.

sentences.en: Payne's is the largest nylon string ball.
sentences.zh: 佩恩的是最大的尼龙绳球。

sentences.en: It's a three-way truce.
sentences.zh: 这是一个三方休战协议。

sentences.en: Except...
sentences.zh: 除了……

sentences.en: Hi!
sentences.zh: 嗨！

sentences.en: JFK?
sentences.zh: JFK？

sentences.en: Hi!
sentences.zh: 嗨！

sentences.en: Um, is it okay if we come over?
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们过去没问题吧？

sentences.en: This is, this is very impressive.
sentences.zh: 这，这太令人印象深刻了。

sentences.en: This is the biggest ball to find in the world.
sentences.zh: 这是世界上能找到的最大的线球。

sentences.en: Of course it is.
sentences.zh: 当然是了。

sentences.en: Yep, there's a fourth ball.
sentences.zh: 没错，还有第四个线球。

sentences.en: And this one is in the Northwoods of Wisconsin.
sentences.zh: 这个位于威斯康星州的北林区。

sentences.en: The man who's rolling it is named James Frank Guterra, but he prefers to go by JFK.
sentences.zh: 滚动它的人叫詹姆斯·弗兰克·古特拉，但他更喜欢别人叫他JFK。

sentences.en: I visited him at the end of my road trip, and he doesn't talk a whole lot, but he has handmade signs posted all over his property with the story of his ball.
sentences.zh: 我在公路旅行结束时拜访了他，他话不多，但在他的地盘上到处都贴着他亲手写的标语，讲述着他这个线球的故事。

sentences.en: He writes that one night, in 1975, God came to him and told him that he was going to stop drinking, turn his life around, and become the world-famous twine man.
sentences.zh: 他写道，1975年的一天晚上，上帝来到他面前，告诉他要戒酒，洗心革面，成为世界闻名的“线球人”。

sentences.en: And that's more or less what he did.
sentences.zh: 他基本上就是这么做的。

sentences.en: Does anybody help you with it at all?
sentences.zh: 有人帮你一起做吗？

sentences.en: No, no.
sentences.zh: 没有，没有。

sentences.en: No one ever helps you.
sentences.zh: 从来没有人帮我。

sentences.en: Just one person, that's JFK.
sentences.zh: 只有一个人，那就是JFK。

sentences.en: And JFK's ball is a little different from the reSt.
sentences.zh: JFK的线球和其他的有点不同。

sentences.en: He takes small segments of colorful twine and weaves and tucks the individual pieces into the ball, so the surface resembles a net.
sentences.zh: 他取来一小段一小段的彩色线，编织并塞进球里，所以表面看起来像个网。

sentences.en: It's also a lot harder for him to reach the top, so the ball's a lot wider than it is tall.
sentences.zh: 对他来说，够到顶部也难得多，所以这个球的宽度远大于高度。

sentences.en: It almost looks like a modern art sculpture.
sentences.zh: 它看起来几乎像一件现代艺术雕塑。

sentences.en: Or a multicolored Funfetti potato.
sentences.zh: 或者一个五颜六色的彩色糖粒土豆。

sentences.en: Well, try and make it as well as you can, but it's hard.
sentences.zh: 嗯，尽量把它做好，但这很难。

sentences.en: And JFK claims that his ball is the largest by using a different metric, weight.
sentences.zh: JFK声称他的线球是最大的，他用的是另一种衡量标准：重量。

sentences.en: 23,375 pounds.
JFK thinks that his ball is about 23,375 pounds, based on his calculations.
sentences.zh: 根据他的计算，JFK认为他的线球大约有23,375磅重。

sentences.en: Nearly 3,000 pounds heavier than Cocker City's.
sentences.zh: 比科克市的那个重了近3000磅。

sentences.en: He says he knows this because before adding twine to the ball, he puts it in a garbage bag, weighs it, and then adds the total to his overall measurements.
sentences.zh: 他说他知道这一点，因为在往球上加线之前，他会把它装进垃圾袋里称重，然后把总数加到他的整体测量数据中。

sentences.en: If he's correct, his is definitely the heaviest of the four twine balls.
sentences.zh: 如果他是对的，那他的绝对是这四个线球中最重的一个。

sentences.en: But JFK's not looking for official records.
sentences.zh: 但JFK并不在乎官方记录。

sentences.en: He doesn't need some outsider to come in and tell him what he already believes.
sentences.zh: 他不需要什么外人跑来告诉他他已经坚信的事情。

sentences.en: Have you heard of the Guinness Book of World Records?
sentences.zh: 你听说过《吉尼斯世界纪录大全》吗？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Are you interested in having them come to measure it at all?
sentences.zh: 你有兴趣让他们来测量一下吗？

sentences.en: No, no, I do it myself.
sentences.zh: 不，不，我自己来。

sentences.en: So you don't really care about what they have to say?
sentences.zh: 所以你并不在乎他们怎么说？

sentences.en: This is mine and mine.
sentences.zh: 这是我的，只属于我。

sentences.en: This is just for you?
sentences.zh: 这只是为你自己做的？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So for now, a careful balance is intact.
sentences.zh: 所以目前，一种微妙的平衡依然存在。

sentences.en: The four largest twine balls exist peacefully alongside one another, each content with their own version of superiority.
sentences.zh: 这四个最大的线球和平共处，每一个都对自己的优越感感到满足。

sentences.en: Because there are so many ways to have the biggest ball of something.
sentences.zh: 因为要成为某种东西的“世界之最”，方法实在太多了。

sentences.en: Like the largest ball of stamps in Boys Town, Nebraska.
sentences.zh: 比如内布拉斯加州男孩镇上最大的邮票球。

sentences.en: Or the largest ball of VHS tape in Kansas City.
sentences.zh: 或者堪萨斯城最大的录像带球。

sentences.en: Or the world's largest disco ball in the UK.
sentences.zh: 又或者英国最大的迪斯科球。

sentences.en: Let it go, Vivian.
sentences.zh: 算了吧，薇薇安。

sentences.en: But what about the world's largest ball of paint in Indiana?
sentences.zh: 那印第安纳州最大的油漆球呢？

sentences.en: It's time to come home.
sentences.zh: 是时候回家了。

sentences.en: I talked to Vivian about other roadside attractions on her Death Defying Midwestern tour after this.
sentences.zh: 之后我和薇薇安聊了聊她那场“勇闯中西部”之旅中其他的路边景点。

sentences.en: So I'm back in the studio with Vivian Lee.
sentences.zh: 我现在又回到了演播室，和薇薇安·李在一起。

sentences.en: And in addition to seeing many, many balls of twine, when we were following along, we were deeply concerned about your safety and well-being.
sentences.zh: 除了看了很多很多线球之外，当我们追踪报道时，我们非常担心你的安全和健康。

sentences.en: I was actually very, I was very concerned about my safety and well-being at the same time.
sentences.zh: 其实我当时也非常，非常担心我自己的安全和健康。

sentences.en: And it's not because of twine.
sentences.zh: 而且这并不是因为线球。

sentences.en: And it was because of the weather.
sentences.zh: 是因为天气。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So apparently, if you're going to plan a reporting trip to a part of the country called Tornado Alley, you should probably check when tornado season is.
sentences.zh: 显然，如果你打算去一个被称为“龙卷风走廊”的地区进行报道旅行，你最好查一下龙卷风季节是什么时候。

sentences.en: Because I happened to be there during the peak of tornado season.
sentences.zh: 因为我刚好是在龙卷风季节的高峰期去了那里。

sentences.en: And there was the most tornado activity since like 2011 or 12 or something.
sentences.zh: 那里的龙卷风活动是自2011年或2012年以来最频繁的。

sentences.en: So tornadoes were landing all around you.
sentences.zh: 所以龙卷风就在你周围着陆。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You didn't see a tornado.
sentences.zh: 你没看到龙卷风吗？

sentences.en: I did not see a tornado.
sentences.zh: 我没看到龙卷风。

sentences.en: I had three weather apps on my phone open at all times.
sentences.zh: 我的手机里一直开着三个天气应用。

sentences.en: And I was tracking the storm and being the exact opposite of Bill Paxton in the movie Twister.
sentences.zh: 我一直在追踪风暴，表现得和电影《龙卷风》里的比尔·帕克斯顿完全相反。

sentences.en: So I would like track the storm and then go as fast as I can the opposite direction.
sentences.zh: 我会追踪风暴，然后以最快的速度朝相反的方向跑。

sentences.en: But like, it was a bummer because I figured I've never been in this part of the country before.
sentences.zh: 但真的很扫兴，因为我想我以前从没去过这个地区。

sentences.en: So I could see, I can make a list of all these roadside attractions that I wanted to see along the way.
sentences.zh: 所以我本来列了一张清单，想看看沿途所有那些路边景点。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So I really wanted to see the Frank Lloyd Wright gas station in Minnesota.
sentences.zh: 我真的很想看明尼苏达州的弗兰克·劳埃德·赖特加油站。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And yeah, and I wanted to see like the world's biggest banjo.
sentences.zh: 我还想看世界上最大的班卓琴之类的东西。

sentences.en: But I just couldn't, I was like rushing from place to place trying to just seek out shelter the entire time because there was thunderstorms and wind.
sentences.zh: 但我实在没法看，我一直在从一个地方赶往另一个地方，试图寻找避难所，因为到处都是雷暴和大风。

sentences.en: It was terrifying.
sentences.zh: 太可怕了。

sentences.en: But one of the places that I really, really wanted to see but just could not get to in time, it was in Lucas, Kansas.
sentences.zh: 但有一个地方我非常非常想看，却没能及时赶到，它在堪萨斯州的卢卡斯。

sentences.en: And it's called The World's Largest Collection of the Smallest Versions of the World's Largest Things.
sentences.zh: 它叫“世界上最大的东西的最小版本收藏馆”。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: You said The World's Largest Collection of the Smallest Versions of the World's Largest Things.
sentences.zh: 你说的是“世界上最大的东西的最小版本收藏馆”。

sentences.en: And it takes a second to really understand, but like everything you need is in the title.
sentences.zh: 这需要一点时间来理解，但标题里已经包含了你需要知道的一切。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So there's all these, there's a lot of different types of roadside attractions, but probably the most popular and the biggest category is like World's Largest Things.
sentences.zh: 路边景点有很多种，但最受欢迎、规模最大的类别大概就是“世界之最”了。

sentences.en: Right, right, right.
sentences.zh: 对，对，对。

sentences.en: So this is basically a collection of miniaturized versions of all the world's largest things in the country.
sentences.zh: 所以这基本上是全国所有“世界之最”事物的微缩版本收藏。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: So there's, there's probably around 400 in the United States.
sentences.zh: 在美国大概有400个这样的东西。

sentences.en: And this woman named Erica Nelson has been basically traveling around and making small versions of all the world's largest roadside attractions that she's seen.
sentences.zh: 一位叫埃里卡·尼尔森的女士一直在四处旅行，并为她见过的所有“世界之最”路边景点制作微缩版本。

sentences.en: And she's an independent artist and educator in Lucas, Kansas.
sentences.zh: 她是堪萨斯州卢卡斯的一位独立艺术家和教育家。

sentences.en: So I was like so fascinated by this that I decided to call her and ask her a little bit about how it works.
sentences.zh: 我对此非常着迷，所以我决定给她打电话，问问她是怎么运作的。

sentences.en: I go to a World's Largest Thing, photograph it, gather its background story.
sentences.zh: 我会去一个“世界之最”景点，拍下照片，收集它的背景故事。

sentences.en: Then I make a World's Smallest Version of that World's Largest Thing and add it to my collection.
sentences.zh: 然后我制作那个“世界之最”的“世界最小版本”，并把它加入我的收藏。

sentences.en: And since I've been doing this for 15 years now, I now have the World's Largest Collection of those World's Smallest Versions of the World's Largest Things.
sentences.zh: 因为我已经做了15年了，我现在拥有了这些“世界之最”事物的“世界最小版本”的最大收藏。

sentences.en: Oh my goodness.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: Oh, I like her.
sentences.zh: 哦，我喜欢她。

sentences.en: She's great.
sentences.zh: 她很棒。

sentences.en: So why in the world did she start doing this?
sentences.zh: 那她到底为什么要开始做这个？

sentences.en: So she would visit these roadside attractions and a lot of times they wouldn't have a gift shop to bring home a souvenir.
sentences.zh: 她会去参观这些路边景点，但很多时候那里没有礼品店可以买纪念品带回家。

sentences.en: So she started making her own souvenirs in the form of these miniaturized versions of these world's largest things.
sentences.zh: 所以她开始制作自己的纪念品，也就是这些“世界之最”事物的微缩版本。

sentences.en: Just for herself.
sentences.zh: 只是为了她自己。

sentences.en: Just for herself.
sentences.zh: 只是为了她自己。

sentences.en: And she's still doing it.
sentences.zh: 而且她还在继续做。

sentences.en: She's still doing it.
sentences.zh: 她还在继续做。

sentences.en: So she still goes to World's Largest Things and still makes new ones.
sentences.zh: 所以她仍然会去参观“世界之最”，并制作新的版本。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So she's hoping to see all 400.
sentences.zh: 她希望能看遍所有400个。

sentences.en: But she has a process where she goes.
sentences.zh: 但她有一套自己的流程。

sentences.en: All 400.
sentences.zh: 全部400个。

sentences.en: Like that's the number of World's Largest Things inside of America.
sentences.zh: 这就是美国境内“世界之最”的数量吗？

sentences.en: It fluctuates.
sentences.zh: 它是在波动的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So there's always more popping up.
sentences.zh: 总是有新的冒出来。

sentences.en: And there's some that are just kind of disappearing from lack of care.
sentences.zh: 也有一些因为缺乏维护而消失了。

sentences.en: Or, you know, people just don't want to maintain them anymore.
sentences.zh: 或者，你知道，人们不再想维护它们了。

sentences.en: So Nelson has like a special affinity for the world's largest things like these types of roadside attractions.
sentences.zh: 所以尼尔森对这些“世界之最”之类的路边景点有一种特殊的偏爱。

sentences.en: But she's also fascinated with roadside attraction culture as a whole.
sentences.zh: 但她也对整个路边景点文化着迷。

sentences.en: And she was telling me that, you know, if you look at it from a historical standpoint,
sentences.zh: 她告诉我，你知道，如果你从历史的角度来看，

sentences.en: you could see the ways in which infrastructure and a push towards car culture have created this environment for roadside attractions to really flourish.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到基础设施和对汽车文化的推动，是如何为路边景点的蓬勃发展创造了环境。

sentences.en: In the 1950s, 1960s, it was also not just our good roads policy, but this interconnectedness that we suddenly felt with our automobiles.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪50年代和60年代，这不仅是因为我们的优质道路政策，还因为我们突然感受到了与汽车之间的这种紧密联系。

sentences.en: And that was really sold to us.
sentences.zh: 而且这确实被推销给了我们。

sentences.en: This is how you get your own personal freedom is by having this machine that can take you as far as you're willing to take it.
sentences.zh: 获得个人自由的方式就是拥有一台机器，它能带你去任何你想去的地方。

sentences.en: So all these little towns popped up in just the right distance to fuel up again or get water again or use the bathroom again or sleep again.
sentences.zh: 所以所有这些小镇都在恰到好处的距离上涌现出来，方便人们加油、取水、上厕所或休息。

sentences.en: But then the interstate system kind of bypassed everything.
sentences.zh: 但后来州际公路系统绕过了所有这些地方。

sentences.en: And all these small towns who had sort of become dependent on slow travel were being bypassed.
sentences.zh: 所有这些曾经依赖慢速旅行的小镇都被绕过了。

sentences.en: And I think those roadside attractions were that way to get people to stop again.
sentences.zh: 我认为那些路边景点就是为了让人们再次停下来而存在的。

sentences.en: So basically, if you don't need to stop in a town for gas or water or to use the bathroom, you have to create something for, you know, the reason why people stop.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，如果你不需要为了加油、取水或上厕所而在一个小镇停留，你就必须创造一些东西，作为人们停留的理由。

sentences.en: That's why you create the world's largest Paul Bunyan statue to pull people off the road.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么你要建造世界上最大的保罗·邦扬雕像来吸引人们下车。

sentences.en: Yes, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: Like if people you'd normally just be completely bypassed.
sentences.zh: 否则人们通常会完全绕过这里。

sentences.en: So it's just a way to keep your economy alive.
sentences.zh: 所以这只是维持经济活力的一种方式。

sentences.en: I'm actually kind of curious about this world's largest phenomenon.
sentences.zh: 我其实对这种“世界之最”现象挺好奇的。

sentences.en: Like, is this just an American thing that we like to make the largest thing possible?
sentences.zh: 这只是美国人才喜欢把东西做得尽可能大吗？

sentences.en: It does seem very distinctly American.
sentences.zh: 这看起来确实非常有美国特色。

sentences.en: Like when I think of the world's largest ball of twine, I don't think I could think of anything more American than that.
sentences.zh: 就像当我想到世界上最大的线球时，我想不出比这更美国的东西了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And you don't think I'm going to go to Switzerland to get the world's largest ball of twine.
sentences.zh: 你肯定不会觉得我会去瑞士看世界上最大的线球。

sentences.en: And our portion sizes are very big.
sentences.zh: 而且我们的份量也很大。

sentences.en: So I would assume the same thing.
sentences.zh: 所以我也会这么认为。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But I actually asked Nelson about this.
sentences.zh: 但我确实问过尼尔森这个问题。

sentences.en: And she says it's not specifically like an American thing, but it's kind of like a new world countries thing.
sentences.zh: 她说这不完全是美国特有的，但这更像是“新世界”国家的一种现象。

sentences.en: I think part of that, that love of superlatives does seem not just an American thing, but a very young country kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 我认为这种对最高级的热爱，似乎不仅仅是美国人的事，而是一个非常年轻的国家会有的那种事。

sentences.en: Because Australia and Canada also have that sort of need to make a mark because we're kind of lacking in that old, old, old history of our built environment.
sentences.zh: 因为澳大利亚和加拿大也有那种想要留下印记的需求，因为我们缺乏那种古老、古老、古老的建筑环境历史。

sentences.en: Because everybody who was here was much more in tune with nature and didn't make giant monuments to themselves.
sentences.zh: 因为曾经在这里的人们更顺应自然，不会为自己建造巨大的纪念碑。

sentences.en: So once we started making our own history, we realized we don't have much.
sentences.zh: 所以当我们开始创造自己的历史时，我们意识到我们并没有多少东西。

sentences.en: So we started doing these superlative things to kind of loud mouth, show offy, say, hey, we're here.
sentences.zh: 所以我们开始做这些追求最高级的事情，大声喧哗、炫耀，说：嘿，我们在这儿。

sentences.en: This is, look at our chicken.
sentences.zh: 这是，看看我们的鸡。

sentences.en: Oh my God.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: Look at our chicken.
sentences.zh: 看看我们的鸡。

sentences.en: So it's because we don't have something like the Pantheon.
sentences.zh: 所以这是因为我们没有像万神殿那样的东西。

sentences.en: We have the world's largest frying pan or something like that.
sentences.zh: 我们有世界上最大的平底锅之类的东西。

sentences.en: Just as good as the Pantheon.
sentences.zh: 和万神殿一样好。

sentences.en: Yeah, but what I think I like most about the world's largest collection of the smallest versions of the world's largest things as a project isn't just that it's, you know,
sentences.zh: 是的，但我认为我最喜欢“世界上最大的东西的最小版本收藏馆”这个项目的地方，不仅仅是因为它，你知道，

sentences.en: a catalog of the biggest things.
sentences.zh: 一个关于最大事物的目录。

sentences.en: It's also a way for Nelson to really explore the stories behind, you know, these small town monuments that aren't traditionally valued from an academic standpoint.
sentences.zh: 这也是尼尔森真正探索这些小镇纪念碑背后故事的一种方式，你知道，这些纪念碑在学术立场上通常并不被重视。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, I guess there isn't the same sort of like academic rigor applied to roadside attractions as there is other forms of vernacular architecture, but there's no reason why not.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我想对于路边景点，确实没有像其他形式的本土建筑那样应用同样的学术严谨性，但没有理由不这样做。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: And Nelson actually says that this attitude is kind of shifting lately.
sentences.zh: 而且尼尔森实际上说，这种态度最近正在发生转变。

sentences.en: I think there's a growing number of people who are who are taking them seriously and have had those debates since learning from Las Vegas came out and ended up being such a tome for architects.
sentences.zh: 我认为越来越多的人开始认真对待它们，并且自从《向拉斯维加斯学习》出版并最终成为建筑师的巨著以来，人们一直在进行这些辩论。

sentences.en: They address that very thing of when is when is Kitsch okay?
sentences.zh: 他们探讨了那个核心问题：媚俗什么时候是可以接受的？

sentences.en: When is populist architecture okay?
sentences.zh: 民粹主义建筑什么时候是可以接受的？

sentences.en: And so with that introduction into scholarly debates, people started looking at them again,
sentences.zh: 因此，随着这些学术辩论的引入，人们开始重新审视它们，

sentences.en: all of these things that they'd grown up around the built environment and reevaluating them in the lenses that they were taught to look at more serious things.
sentences.zh: 所有这些他们从小就在周围看到的建筑环境，并用他们被教导去审视更严肃事物的视角来重新评估它们。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And we covered a lot of this stuff in a story Avery did about Denise Scott Brown and Robert Venturi about, you know, learning from Las Vegas.
sentences.zh: 我们在艾弗里关于丹妮丝·斯科特·布朗和罗伯特·文丘里的报道中涵盖了大部分内容，你知道，就是关于《向拉斯维加斯学习》那本书。

sentences.en: I mean, this idea that, you know,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这个想法，你知道，

sentences.en: they became really advocates for the architecture of Las Vegas that most people and even people like I performed in Las Vegas for the AIA conference and somebody wrote me to say,
sentences.zh: 他们真正成为了拉斯维加斯建筑的倡导者，而大多数人，甚至像我这样的人——我曾在拉斯维加斯的美国建筑师协会会议上演讲，有人写信给我说，

sentences.en: I can't believe we're doing it in Las Vegas.
sentences.zh: 我不敢相信我们竟然在拉斯维加斯举办会议。

sentences.en: There is nothing of value there.
sentences.zh: 那里根本没有任何价值。

sentences.en: And I was like, there's like, there's like a whole book about it.
sentences.zh: 我就说，那里可是有一整本书专门讲这个的。

sentences.en: And in that episode, you should listen to our episode.
sentences.zh: 在那一集里，你应该听听我们那一集。

sentences.en: For a long time, we've turned around this thinking.
sentences.zh: 很长一段时间以来，我们已经扭转了这种想法。

sentences.en: And, you know, in general, we should think about what people go to, you know, because, you know, that's worth evaluating why they want to be in places like Las Vegas.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，总的来说，我们应该思考人们去往何处，你知道，因为，你知道，评估他们为什么想去拉斯维加斯这样的地方是值得的。

sentences.en: I mean, it really does teach us something.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它确实教会了我们一些东西。

sentences.en: Yes, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: Like that, that demand is there for a reason.
sentences.zh: 就像那样，这种需求的存在是有原因的。

sentences.en: And, you know, like a giant fiberglass pheasant or a twine ball might, I mean, yes, it's silly and it comes off as silly,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，比如一个巨大的玻璃纤维野鸡或一个麻绳球，我的意思是，是的，它很傻，看起来也很傻，

sentences.en: but people are drawn to these stories and stories behind them and the people who've made these objects, because it tells you a lot about, you know,
sentences.zh: 但人们被这些故事、故事背后的故事以及制作这些物品的人所吸引，因为它告诉了你很多关于，你知道，

sentences.en: the region and the people who live there.
sentences.zh: 那个地区以及住在那里的人们的信息。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, since they were a reaction to the way that we travel and as we were beginning to bypass a lot of these towns and they became attractions for those reasons,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，因为它们是对我们旅行方式的一种反应，而且随着我们开始绕过许多这些城镇，它们因为这些原因成为了景点，

sentences.en: are roadside attractions continuing to evolve as travel evolves?
sentences.zh: 路边景点是否随着旅行方式的演变而继续进化？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I, I asked, I asked Nelson this question because, you know, we're, we're not in like the rapid expansion phase of road travel anymore.
sentences.zh: 我问了尼尔森这个问题，因为，你知道，我们不再处于公路旅行的快速扩张阶段了。

sentences.en: You know, for the past few decades, we've been doing air travel and, you know, with climate change, we're kind of more aware of our carbon footprints.
sentences.zh: 你知道，过去几十年我们一直在进行航空旅行，而且，你知道，随着气候变化，我们对自己的碳足迹有了更多的了解。

sentences.en: And also there's, you know, a little, a little bit more, a little more aware of our carbon footprints.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，稍微，稍微多了解了一点我们的碳足迹。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: A little bit.
sentences.zh: 一点点。

sentences.en: We're trying.
sentences.zh: 我们正在努力。

sentences.en: But like, yeah.
sentences.zh: 但是，是的。

sentences.en: The world's largest ball of carbon.
sentences.zh: 世界上最大的碳球。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: We've got that.
sentences.zh: 我们有那个。

sentences.en: We definitely have that.
sentences.zh: 我们绝对有那个。

sentences.en: But yeah, I asked her about this because, because I was kind of curious and it's still, it's still a little bit of a question mark.
sentences.zh: 但是，是的，我问她这个问题是因为，因为我有点好奇，而且这仍然，仍然是一个问号。

sentences.en: I'm not sure yet.
sentences.zh: 我还不确定。

sentences.en: I mean, will there be a whole new set that's around mass rail or artwork in airports has really exploded too.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，会不会有一整套围绕大众铁路的新景点，或者机场里的艺术品也确实爆发式增长了。

sentences.en: Artwork has happened in that controlled environment, but roadside attractions don't really have an inlet there yet because they're, they're so controlled.
sentences.zh: 艺术品在那种受控环境中出现了，但路边景点在那里还没有真正的切入点，因为它们，它们太受控了。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: Would there be a, a slow version in cities that's just alleyway embellishments that the new roadside is the sidewalk, a little tiny thing on your path to, to the next Starbucks?
sentences.zh: 城市里会不会有一个慢节奏的版本，只是小巷的装饰，新的路边景点就是人行道，在你去下一家星巴克的路上的一点点小东西？

sentences.en: I think that that's right on the money.
sentences.zh: 我觉得你说得太对了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, just because like, there's all these types of little artistic interventions in urban landscapes and maybe they've always been there.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，仅仅因为，城市景观中有各种各样的小型艺术干预，也许它们一直都在那里。

sentences.en: I don't know if they, they function as attractions exactly, but they are about embedding art in the built world.
sentences.zh: 我不知道它们是否完全作为景点发挥作用，但它们确实是关于将艺术嵌入建筑世界。

sentences.en: And that seems like that impulse is there, but she's definitely right about airport art.
sentences.zh: 这种冲动似乎确实存在，但她在机场艺术方面的看法绝对是正确的。

sentences.en: Like I travel a lot these days and airport art is really good.
sentences.zh: 比如我最近经常旅行，机场的艺术真的很棒。

sentences.en: Exhibits at SFO and exhibit in the mural at the Oakland airport are just stunning.
sentences.zh: 旧金山国际机场的展览和奥克兰机场的壁画展览简直令人惊叹。

sentences.en: I love them.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢它们。

sentences.en: And I look forward to seeing them.
sentences.zh: 我很期待看到它们。

sentences.en: For a while there was like old board games and it was just like an exhibit of old board games in SFO.
sentences.zh: 有一段时间，旧金山国际机场有旧棋盘游戏的展览，就像是一个旧棋盘游戏的展览。

sentences.en: And I would totally stop at that museum.
sentences.zh: 我绝对会停下来参观那个博物馆。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I would.
sentences.zh: 我会的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: If it was, you know, like on the side of the road in Kansas, I totally would go to the old board game museum in Kansas.
sentences.zh: 如果它，你知道，在堪萨斯州的路边，我绝对会去堪萨斯州的旧棋盘游戏博物馆。

sentences.en: Well, that's great.
sentences.zh: 好吧，那太棒了。

sentences.en: I'm glad you didn't die.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴你没死。

sentences.en: I'm really glad I didn't die too.
sentences.zh: 我也很高兴我没死。

sentences.en: Thank you for saying that.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你这么说。

sentences.en: But one last thing about the world's largest version, wait, the world's, I don't think I could do this.
sentences.zh: 但关于世界上最大的版本，最后一件事，等等，世界上最大的，我不认为我能做到这一点。

sentences.zh: 世界上最大的“世界上最大的事物”的最小版本收藏，它们有一首主题曲。

sentences.en: Oh.
sentences.zh: 哦。

sentences.en: And I would love to play that.
sentences.zh: 我很想播放那首歌。

sentences.en: Oh, let's do it.
sentences.zh: 哦，我们来吧。

sentences.en: Let's do this.
sentences.zh: 我们来做吧。

sentences.en: We'll go out on this.
sentences.zh: 我们以这个结束。

sentences.en: Thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.zh: 我没疯，但有一头巨大的会说话的牛，它在跟我说话。
